Title: Models API reference
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/api-documentation/api-actions
Content: The API for interacting with models is extensive. It includes several endpoints and methods for retrieving, creating, and updating model content and associated metadata.

Note that a comprehensive reference that lists all API endpoints, methods, and schemas can be found on our Swagger site, which can be accessed via the Help section inside Solidatus (you need to be logged in to access this documentation).
Title: API Model building tutorial
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/solidatus-6.5/api-documentation/api-overview/api-model-building-tutorial
Content: Create relationships between your lineage model entities and terms in reference models using the SetRelationship command. You will need IDs of the lineage entity, reference model, and reference term you want to relate to.

Add a relationship to a data governance term

curl -X POST \
  --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer API_TOKEN" \
  --data '{
    "cmds": [
      {
        "cmd": "SetRelationship",
        "id": "entity ID of customers table",
        "referenceModelId": "ID of your reference model",
        "termId": "ID of PII classification term",
        "label": "is classified as"
      }
    ],
    "commit": true,
    "commitMessage": "Add PII classification relationship"
  }' \
  SOLIDATUS_URL/api/v1/models/MODEL_ID/update

Title: Reference model interface
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/the-user-interface/models-ui/build-reference-models
Content: To create a reference model, click the Create button on the Model Browser and select Reference model:

Create a reference model

When creating a reference model, you can indicate its prupose by choosing a reference model type; you should also provide a description for the model to help other users (or the AI assistant) understand it.

A Reference Model is more than just a name

A reference model’s type can be changed at any time by editing the model information in the Settings tab in the Reference Model Overview.

Note that selecting a type of Reference model just adds a label and changes its icon in the model list; it does not the affect how the model functions.

Adding additional tags to the model can also be useful for classification purposes.
Title: Reference models 101
Link: https://docs.solidatus.com/models/understand-solidatus-models/reference-models-101
Content: Solidatus allows you to indicate the purpose of a Reference Model by selecting from a list of types:

Asset Inventory
Business Glossary
Data Dictionary

However, choosing a type makes no difference to how the Reference Model will work; it’s just a label, and all Reference model types function in the same way.

Choosing a type makes it easy to identify the purpose and content of a Reference Model, as the type is displayed in the list of models in the Model Browser, and also when creating or viewing Reference Relationships.

A Reference Model’s type can be changed at any time by editing model information in the Settings tab in the Model Overview of a Reference model.
